html:
The Nisga'a are a Tsimshianic-speaking people of the Nass River valley in northwestern British Columbia. The Nass was famous for its spring run of oolichan, a small oily fish. People came from far along the coast to trade for its grease, which was carried inland along "grease trails".

Like the Tsimshian and Haida, they lived in cedar houses grouped into clans, held potlatch feasts and raised tall totem poles.

The Nisga'a fought for their land in the courts and in politics for over a century. Their case, Calder v British Columbia, led the Supreme Court of Canada to say in 1973 that Aboriginal title to land existed in law. In 2000 the Nisga'a Treaty came into force, the first modern treaty in British Columbia, giving them self-government over about 2,000 square kilometres of the Nass valley.
